principles.title: General Principles
principles.body: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) came into effect on May 25, 2018. All companies, including management companies, are required to comply with this European regulation by ensuring respect for the rights of data subjects. The previous system, based on CNIL oversight through a declaratory regime via prior declarations (cf. Data Protection Act of 1978), has been abolished. It is now a logic of accountability based on a risk-based approach. Companies must ensure that all persons whose personal data is processed are informed about the type of information collected, how the company uses this information, the retention period for this data, and the possibility of requesting modification or deletion. This compliance first requires mapping or inventorying all files containing personal information, both internal (e.g., employees) and external (clients, service providers…), ensuring the security of this data, and being able to justify it at any time. The company must have all data subjects accept its data processing policy.

framework.title: Regulatory Framework
framework.body: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation).

objectives.title: Objectives
objectives.body:
This data processing policy aims to clarify and establish the framework applicable to all personal data held by MANCO.PARIS. It distinguishes between internal data processing (employees in particular) and external data (clients, service providers…). The implementation of the GDPR concretely involves for MANCO.PARIS:

• The appointment of a data processing and monitoring officer: The designated person is Jérôme COIRIER – He can be contacted at: dpo@manco.paris.
• The establishment of a personal data processing register to inventory personal data collected and its purposes.
• The implementation of a general data and cookie processing policy available on our website for user information.
• Information at the time of account creation about our personal data processing policy, user rights, and data usage.
• Information to all our clients and service providers about our general personal data processing policy.

dataCollected.title: Data Collected
dataCollected.body: Data collected relates to identification (surname, first name, postal address, phone number, email address, company), professional, economic or financial situation (position held within the company, client categorization…). The client is informed of their rights at the time of data collection and throughout the duration of the contract.

dataUse.title: Use of Data
dataUse.body: MANCO.PARIS collects your personal data solely in the context of your information requests and our commercial exchanges. This data is used exclusively by MANCO.PARIS to inform you about its activities.

registry.title: Record Keeping
registry.body: A register is maintained by the management company under the oversight of the data processing and monitoring officer. This register classifies and inventories all personal data collected by the company.

rights.title: Information on Your Rights
rights.body:
In accordance with current regulations, you have:

• The right of access to personal data concerning you
• The right to rectification, modification or erasure thereof
• The right to restriction of processing relating to this personal data
• The right to object to processing (unless necessary to comply with our legal and regulatory obligations)
• The right to data portability
• The right to lodge a complaint with the CNIL

Information on your rights is communicated via our website's data processing updates.

retention.title: Personal Data Retention Period
retention.body:
Personal data cannot be stored indefinitely in digital files. Your personal data will be retained throughout the business relationship and deleted after a period of three years following our last exchange in the absence of a business relationship.

However, there are cases where your data may be retained longer:
• To meet legal, accounting or tax obligations (10 years)
• For the preservation of evidence during applicable limitation periods (5 years)

contactDpo.title: Contact Us
contactDpo.body:
You may address any complaint regarding the processing of your personal data by email to the data processing and monitoring officer at: dpo@manco.paris, or by post to: MANCO.PARIS, 7 rue Roy 75008 PARIS.

If dissatisfied with the processing of your personal data, you may lodge a complaint in France with the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (C.N.I.L) at: Service des plaintes, 3 Place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715 – 75334 Paris Cedex 07 – 01 53 73 22 22 – www.cnil.fr/fr/plaintes

purpose.title: Purpose of the Website
purpose.body:
The Manco Paris website is strictly informational, aiming to present asset management activities. All information available on the site is exclusively indicative. This is not a transactional website.

Any information may be modified without prior notice by the company. Under no circumstances does information published on the site represent an offer of products or services that could be considered a public savings offer, or canvassing or solicitation to buy or sell any management or investment product.

responsibilities.title: Liability
responsibilities.body:
Manco Paris strives to ensure the accuracy and timeliness of information published on this site, and reserves the right to correct content at any time without prior notice.

We advise visitors to verify information through other means, including by contacting us. Consequently, we disclaim all liability: for any inaccuracy, inexactitude or omission regarding information available on the site; for any damage resulting from a fraudulent intrusion by a third party that led to modification of information made available on the site.

External sites linked to Manco.paris are not under its control, and it consequently disclaims all liability for their content. These links do not constitute approval or partnership between the company and these sites, which are subject to their own terms of use and privacy policies.

Any dissemination or reference to external documents shall mention at least:
— the source of information and the period to which the information relates
— whether it is an extract or the entirety of a document
— the origin, date and references of the document

Before setting up any such links, you must request permission from Manco Paris. Your request should be addressed to the company at its registered office or by filling out our contact form.

vote.title: Voting Policy
vote.body: As MANCO.PARIS does not carry out financial management activities on its own behalf, the voting policy as defined by article 321-132 of the AMF General Regulation does not apply to the company.

esg.title: ESG Policy
esg.body:
Article 173 of the Energy Transition for Green Growth Act n°2015-992 of August 17, 2015 amends Article L. 533-22-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code, which now provides that "management companies shall make available to subscribers of each of the UCIs they manage information on how their investment policy takes into account criteria relating to compliance with social, environmental and governance quality objectives. They specify the nature of these criteria and how they apply them according to a standard presentation established by decree. They indicate how they exercise the voting rights attached to the financial instruments resulting from these choices."

As MANCO.PARIS does not carry out financial management or investment activities on its own behalf, it cannot formally integrate criteria related to social, environmental, or governance objectives. However, MANCO.PARIS pays particular attention to the consideration of these criteria in the investment processes of the management companies to which it delegates fund management.

MANCO.PARIS and the UCIs whose financial management it delegates have not, to date, adhered to any charter, code, initiative or label relating to the consideration of ESG criteria.

sfdr.title: Sustainability Risk Policy
sfdr.body:
Article 3 of EU Regulation n°2019/2088 (SFDR) on sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector provides that all financial sector actors may develop a general policy on the integration of sustainability risks into their operations.

As MANCO.PARIS does not carry out financial management activities on its own behalf, it cannot integrate sustainability risks as such. However, in the context of its service activities for management companies, it ensures that these companies begin to take these risks into account in their investment decisions, particularly risks associated with climate and biodiversity. Similarly, it ensures that the regulatory documents of delegated funds comply with the obligations for funds described in Articles 9 and 8. Finally, it ensures that the remuneration policies of delegated companies take sustainability risks into account for populations involved in management decisions. Regarding investment advisory activities, MANCO.PARIS does not currently take sustainability risks into account.

Article 5 of EU Regulation n°2019/2088 (SFDR) on sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector provides that remuneration policies within management companies encourage or do not discourage the consideration of sustainability risks in investment decision-making or investment advisory processes. As MANCO.PARIS does not carry out financial management activities on its own behalf, it cannot integrate sustainability risks into its remuneration policy. However, its employees are encouraged to take sustainability risks into account in their activities.

The remuneration policy of MANCO.PARIS is summarized on the website www.manco-paris.com

claims.title: Client Complaints Handling
claims.body:
In accordance with applicable regulatory requirements (cf. art. 321-40 of the AMF General Regulation), MANCO.PARIS has established and maintains an operational procedure for the effective handling of client complaints (this procedure is available free of charge upon request from MANCO.PARIS).

Any complaint may be sent to the following email address: claim@manco.paris, or by post to: MANCO.PARIS, complaints department, 7 rue Roy, 75008 Paris. Management will make every effort to respond to your request as soon as possible and in any case within a maximum period of two months from receipt of your request.

In the event of a persistent disagreement, you may contact a mediator, including the AMF mediator. The AMF mediator's contact details are: Autorité des marchés financiers, Médiateur de l'AMF, 17 place de la Bourse 75082 PARIS CEDEX 02. The AMF mediation request form and the mediation charter are available at http://www.amf-france.org.

conflicts.title: Conflicts of Interest Policy
conflicts.body:
MANCO.PARIS takes all necessary measures to detect conflicts of interest situations that may arise in the course of its activities: UCITS or AIF management, investment advisory, support services.

In accordance with current regulations, MANCO.PARIS has a conflicts of interest management policy.

This policy sets out the procedures to follow and measures to take to manage conflicts of interest situations, with the objective of prioritizing client interest and maintaining market integrity.

This policy can be obtained upon request from the management company.

In accordance with regulatory provisions, MANCO.PARIS maintains an up-to-date register recording, as needed, potential conflicts of interest.

In the presence of a proven conflict of interest, MANCO.PARIS informs the client of the situation identified and the measures envisaged. Information provided to clients will be archived.

Furthermore, the identification of conflicts of interest has led to the development of a conflicts of interest map. This map identifies situations that give rise or are likely to give rise to a conflict of interest. It enables the detection and, where applicable, fair management of conflicts of interest that may arise in the course of its services, between its own interests and those of its clients, or between the interests of several clients.

This notably includes the identification and monitoring of:
• employee participation in one or more investment services offered by the management company
• separation of activities likely to generate potential conflicts
• circulation of confidential or privileged information within the management company
• corporate mandates held by management company employees privately or in connection with their professional activities
• commissions paid or received for services or activities carried out by or for the management company
• benefits or gifts potentially received by management company employees in connection with their professional activities
• risks of conflicts of interest situations in the intermediary and service provider selection process
• implementation of an incident management procedure to preserve the primacy of client interest
• implementation of a personal transactions procedure
• implementation of a gifts given and/or received from clients and service providers procedure

bestSelection.title: Best Selection Policy
bestSelection.body:
Investment service providers must take all reasonable measures to obtain, when executing orders, the best possible result for their clients taking into account price, cost, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement/delivery, the nature of orders... and all other considerations relating to execution.

MANCO.PARIS does not carry out financial management activities on its own behalf and therefore does not select financial intermediaries.
